column1: # One row per name, in each source's own order (pos): father to son, except
# Luke, son to father. in_descent says how a row joins the line: "yes", the
# neighbouring row is this person's father; "unstated", the person belongs here
# but the text does not state that link (1 Chr 3:18's Pedaiah, listed after
# Shealtiel among Jeconiah's descendants; the separate Ezra and Haggai
# statements); "skip", not a link of descent at all (the kings_judah succession
# list's Athaliah, a queen mother, Jehoahaz, a brother, and Zedekiah, an uncle;
# Luke's closing "son of God"). Transcribed from the BSB (public domain); every
# name was checked against its cited verse and against STEPBible's tagged text.
# Who is the same person across sources is in genealogy-people.tsv. Open issues:

Listed among “the sons of Israel”. Brothers (2:1-2): Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, Asher.
“Tamar, Judah’s daughter-in-law, bore to him Perez and Zerah.” Twin brother Zerah; half-brothers Er, Onan, Shelah (2:3).
“The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.” Brother Hamul.
“The sons who were born to Hezron: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.” Brothers Jerahmeel and Caleb (BSB footnote: “Hebrew Chelubai, a variant of Caleb; see verse 18.”).
“a leader of the descendants of Judah”.
BSB footnote: “LXX (see also Ruth 4:20–21); Hebrew Salma; twice in this verse”.
“and David seventh”. Brothers (2:13-15): Eliab, Abinadab, Shimea, Nethanel, Raddai, Ozem; sisters Zeruiah and Abigail (2:16).

BSB footnote: “Azariah is also called Uzziah; see 2 Chronicles 26:1.”

“Johanan was the firstborn, Jehoiakim the second, Zedekiah the third, and Shallum the fourth.” Brothers: Johanan, Zedekiah, Shallum (BSB footnote: “Shallum is another name for Jehoahaz.”). The line continues through Jehoiakim: “The successors of Jehoiakim” (1 Chr 3:16). Omitted by Matthew.

“Jeconiah his son, and Zedekiah.” BSB footnote: “Jeconiah is a variant of Jehoiachin; also in verse 17; see 2 Kings 24:6.” The Zedekiah listed with him is not followed further; whether he is a son of Jehoiakim or the uncle of 3:15 is not stated.

“The descendants of Jeconiah the captive: Shealtiel his son,”. Verse 18 continues the same list: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, Nedabiah, read most naturally as Shealtiel's brothers. The chapter does not continue Shealtiel's own line: it continues through Pedaiah (3:19).

Listed in the descendants of Jeconiah after Shealtiel: “Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.” The text does NOT say Pedaiah is Shealtiel's son, so pos 19 -> 20 is list order, not a stated father-son link. Brothers: Shealtiel, Malchiram, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, Nedabiah.
1 Chr 3:19 names Pedaiah as Zerubbabel's father: “The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei.” Contrast “Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel” (Ezra 3:2) and Matt 1:12. Brother Shimei.

“The children of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah, their sister Shelomith,” then “five others: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-hesed” (1 Chr 3:20). The line continues through Hananiah (3:21). Neither Abiud (Matt 1:13) nor Rhesa (Luke 3:27) is listed.

“The descendants of Hananiah: Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, and the sons of Rephaiah, of Arnan, of Obadiah, and of Shecaniah.” Shecaniah's exact relation to Hananiah is not stated. Co-listed: Pelatiah, Jeshaiah, Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah. The line continues through Shecaniah (3:22).
“The six descendants of Shecaniah were Shemaiah and his sons”.
“Shemaiah and his sons: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat.” Brothers: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Shaphat. The line continues through Neariah (3:23).

“The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam—three in all.” Brothers: Hizkiah, Azrikam. His seven sons end the chapter and are not followed further: “Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani—seven in all.” (1 Chr 3:24)
“This is the book of the generations of Adam.”
“And he named him Noah”. Lamech “had a son” (Gen 5:28) without naming him.
“he became the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Only Shem is recorded as the line (it continues in Gen 11:10); brothers Ham and Japheth.
“This is the account of Shem.”
“When Arphaxad was 35 years old, he became the father of Shelah.” No Cainan between Arphaxad and Shelah (contrast Luke 3:36).

Queen, Ahaziah's mother: “Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah” (2 Kgs 11:1). Ruled six years: “for six years while Athaliah ruled the land.” A usurper, not a descendant of David; not a link in any genealogy here. Exclude when comparing with Matthew's father-son list.

Son of Amon: “they made his son Josiah king in his place.” Also 2 Kgs 21:26.
“Jehoahaz son of Josiah”. Reigned three months (2 Kgs 23:31). A brother of Jehoiakim, not in the line to Jeconiah; = Shallum of 1 Chr 3:15 per the BSB footnote there.
“Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim son of Josiah king in place of his father Josiah, and he changed Eliakim’s name to Jehoiakim.” Brother of Jehoahaz. Omitted by Matthew.
Son of Jehoiakim: “his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.” = Jeconiah (BSB footnote at 1 Chr 3:16).
“the king of Babylon made Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, king in his place and changed his name to Zedekiah.” A son of Josiah (1 Chr 3:15); not in the line to Jeconiah.
